non_blocking.finding: The revised rule for attributing an odom_stale end measures the lag from the newest pose received at or before data.stop_flow.started_monotonic_s. The recorded runs show that pose is often not the one the gate tripped on. The runtime's monitor thread polls the gate every 50 ms, so a stop flow can start after the pose gap has already ended. That happened in 4 of the 9 recorded odom_stale ends: v17_building_route01 (the flow started 6 ms after the gap ended), v25_historical_full01 (4 ms), v30_historical_full01 (41 ms) and diag_v31_clock03 (12 ms). There the rule measures 0.001-0.025 s from a pose delivered after the gap, instead of 0.27-0.30 s from the gap's start. So under v33, if the pose path resumes within one monitor period of a backstop trip, the rule assigns the trip to the simulation age. The misattribution would at least show as an impossibly small lag. My round-2 suggestion ('minus the entered time of the newest pose') introduced this gap in the rule. The stated rationale for the threshold, '1.98 s (2.0 s less one 20 ms watchdog tick)', points the wrong way. The backstop trips only once now minus monotonic_s exceeds 2.0 s, and the stop flow starts after the trip, so a backstop lag always exceeds 2.0 s. The watchdog can only add delay. The round-2 counterexample (a simulation-age trip followed by continued pose loss) is now handled correctly.
non_blocking.evidence: PHYSICAL_RUN_PLAN.md:75-79; PLAN.md:302-305; runtime_sources/backend_ros/p2b_backend_ros/runtime.py:271-281 (monitor_period_s 0.05); reviewer scratch stop-flow timing over the recorded runs: the flow started inside the gap for v28, v31, v32, diag_v31_clock04 and diag_v32_clock01, and after the gap ended for the four runs named.
non_blocking.suggestion: Before the freeze, take the lag from the start of the newest pose gap over 0.25 s that contains the stop flow's start, or that ended at most one monitor period plus margin (for example 0.1 s) before it. Call it the backstop if and only if that lag is at least 2.0 s. Report the observer's /clock at the stop flow's start as a cross-check.
